newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Freightforward Europe issues white paper.
newsitem.headline: Freightforward Europe issues white paper.

text.p: FreightForward Europe, a group representing nine major freight forwarders, has issued a White Paper which aims to stress the increasing role of the forwarder in airfreight transport.

The White Paper called "From agent to global logistics provider:the changing role of the airfreight forwarder", states how the forwarders see their role becoming more important through long-term and mutually beneficial partnerships with both shippers and airlines.

FFE claims that forwarders will surpass the benchmarks set by the integrators by providing multimodality, total control and documentation services and by tailoring their services to respond directly to shippers needs.
The forwarding group adds that these measures will prevent shippers from having to make costly investments in specialised communications technology.

FFE expects the global air cargo market to grow by seven to ten percent per year over the next few years. However, the need for integrated global logistics solutions will lead to a consolidation in the freight forwarding industry, it states.
Major multinational forwarders will also aim to accelerate the development of advanced technology in air freight, the group added.
The nine forwarders point out that 80 percent of the airline business is passenger driven and that freight is still not a sufficient priority.
As forwarders focus on freight they can help airlines improve their services and cut their costs by streamlining procedures and this will ultimately benefit the shipper, the group stated.
They also argue that airlines are still multinationals working from their home bases whereas forwarders are truly global operators.
FFE expects its members to increase the volumes of their business which depend on providing logistics solutions tailored to shippers' individual supply chain needs.

Forwarders and airlines are building long-term partnerships based on an understanding of each other's core skills, it states. The FFE highlights the honouring of space commitments by the forwarder, rebates based on the forwarder's performance, and an emphasis on having as little loose cargo as possible.
Kuehne & Nagel, Panalpina, Schenker-Rhenus, Thyssen Haniel Logistic, ASG, Bilspedition, Dachser, Danzas and LEP are the FFE members.
